mainTopic: Fulfilling פריה ורביה through children and grandchildren, continuing to have children in old age, and the value of marriage
overview: The גמרא finishes testing רב הונא, who said a man whose children died has still done פריה ורביה. A ברייתא saying a child who died does not count refutes him. Next comes the question of which grandchildren count. אביי limits it, but רבא says any grandchildren who keep the world populated are enough. Everyone agrees, though, that two grandchildren from one child are not enough, and the story of רב ששת does not change that. The source for 'grandchildren are like children' is found in the פסוקים about מכיר. The גמרא then brings רבי יהושע, who says a man should keep having children even in old age, and רב מתנא rules like him. Along the way comes רבי עקיבא's teaching to keep teaching in old age, with the story of his 24,000 students who died. The amud ends with sayings praising marriage and a husband's duties to his wife and family.

steps.title: Grandchildren are like children: a challenge to רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying grandchildren count like children, to challenge רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grandchildren are like children!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short ברייתא to push back on רב הונא, who said that a man whose children died has still done the מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grandchildren only matter because they stand in for children, it sounds like the man's own children who died do not count by themselves. So it seems he needs living descendants, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Like children: they count the same
The מצוה to be fruitful and multiply

phrases.english: Grandchildren are like children!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to רב הונא from the end of the previous daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that one who had children who died has fulfilled פריה ורביה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא suggests grandchildren are needed to replace dead children, so dead children by themselves would not be enough.

steps.title: The ברייתא is only about completing the count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about grandchildren filling in a missing child, not replacing children who died.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about completing the count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the ברייתא more narrowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא means grandchildren can fill in what is missing. For example, a man with only a son, whose son has a daughter, now has 'a son and a daughter.' It says nothing about a man whose children died, so רב הונא is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: To complete: to fill in a missing child

phrases.english: When that was taught, it was for completing.
phrases.notes: He means completing the required son and daughter. For example, a son's daughter can fill in for a missing daughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grandchildren replace children who died, so dead children do not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grandchildren only fill in a missing child; the ברייתא does not discuss children who died.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a child who died does not count
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says outright that if one of the children died, the father has not fulfilled the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Grandchildren are like children. If one of them died or was found to be a סריס, he has not fulfilled פריה ורביה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger ברייתא that clearly argues against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא states openly that if a child dies, the father has not done the מצוה. That cannot be explained away as being about 'completing,' so it contradicts רב הונא directly.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who cannot have children

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי: בְּנֵי בָנִים הֲרֵי הֵם כְּבָנִים,
phrases.english: They challenged: Grandchildren are like children.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת אֶחָד מֵהֶם אוֹ שֶׁנִּמְצָא סָרִיס —
phrases.english: If one of them died, or was found to be a eunuch,
he has not fulfilled being fruitful and multiplying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 2 saved רב הונא, this brings a clearer source against him.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly says a child who died does not count, which is the exact opposite of רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares רב הונא's view refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רב הונא is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the challenge has no answer, so רב הונא's view is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the ברייתא clearly says a child who died does not count, רב הונא's opinion cannot stand. The הלכה follows the view that the man needs living children or grandchildren.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation: a challenge with no answer

steps.whatToRemember: A man whose children died has not fulfilled פריה ורביה; רב הונא's opposite view is refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rav Huna is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 3 with no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is refuted: children who died do not count toward פריה ורביה.

steps.title: אביי: which grandchildren count
steps.stepSummary: אביי thinks a grandchild only replaces a child if it matches the child, or is a son in place of a daughter, but a son's daughter does not replace the son.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grandchildren are like children. אביי thought to say: a son to a son, a daughter to a daughter, and certainly a son to a daughter. But a daughter to a son, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the phrase 'grandchildren are like children' and asks which grandchildren count. אביי gives his first idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the grandchild has to 'stand in' for its parent: a son's son replaces the son, a daughter's daughter replaces the daughter. A daughter's son is even better, since a son is the more central part of the מצוה. A son's daughter cannot replace the son.

keyTerms.meaning: He thought to say (a first idea that may be rejected)

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר אביי למימר' tells you this is only אביי's first idea. רבא is about to reject it.

phrases.english: Grandchildren are like children.
Abaye thought to say:
a son to a son, and a daughter to a daughter,
phrases.notes: He means a son born to his son, and a daughter born to his daughter.

phrases.english: and all the more so a son to a daughter.
But a daughter to a son, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: defining which grandchildren count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grandchildren count only if each stands in for a parent of the same gender or a better one (a son for a daughter), not a daughter for a son.

steps.title: רבא: the goal is a populated world
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי: what matters is 'לשבת יצרה,' and any grandchildren do that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: We need 'He formed it to be inhabited,' and that is present here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's limit and says the gender of the grandchild does not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לשבת יצרה' teaches that the point of the מצוה is to fill the world with people. As long as the man has descendants who keep the world inhabited, a son's daughter counts too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He formed it to be inhabited': the world was made to be lived in

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the מצוה is measured by its goal, filling the world, not by an exact match of genders between children and grandchildren.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
We need 'He formed it to be inhabited,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 45:18

phrases.english: and that is present.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's limitation in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's exclusion of a son's daughter
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי focused on matching genders, but the real requirement is only that the world be populated.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: two grandchildren from one child are not enough
steps.stepSummary: Both אביי and רבא agree that two grandchildren from only one child do not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: At least according to everyone, two from one do not count.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes a point that both אביי and רבא agree on. This also sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even רבא, who is lenient about gender, needs the grandchildren to come from two different children. A grandson and granddaughter from the same child are not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Two from one: two grandchildren from one child

phrases.english: According to everyone, at least,
two from one, no.
phrases.notes: He means two grandchildren who both come from the same child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out common ground between אביי and רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two grandchildren from a single child do not fulfill פריה ורביה, according to both opinions.

steps.title: רב ששת: my daughter's sons are my sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the point that 'two from one' does not count, using רב ששת's answer to the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not? But the רבנן said to רב ששת: Marry a woman and have sons. And he said to them: The sons of my daughter are my sons!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the claim from step 7 by bringing a story about רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת seems to have had only a daughter, yet he said her sons counted as his sons for the מצוה. That looks like 'two from one' does count, which goes against what everyone agreed in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: And not?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: But the Rabbis said to Rav Sheshet:
Marry a woman and have sons,
and he said to them:
The sons of my daughter are my sons!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא? וְהָא אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the shared position stated in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The agreed rule that two grandchildren from one child do not count
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ששת relied on grandchildren from his one daughter to fulfill the מצוה, which suggests 'two from one' is enough.

steps.title: רב ששת was only giving an excuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from רב ששת: his claim that his daughter's children counted was only a way to put off the רבנן. His real reason was that he had become unable to have children.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he was just putting them off. The real reason was that רב ששת had become impotent from sitting through רב הונא's long lectures.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 8. It says רב ששת's answer to the רבנן was not his real reasoning, so we cannot learn a הלכה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge used רב ששת's words to show that 'two from one child' might count. The גמרא now says those words were only an excuse. Since he could not have more children anyway, his statement proves nothing, and the rule from step 7 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: he was just putting them off (giving an excuse)
became uprooted, meaning he became impotent
a public lecture given by a rabbi

steps.confusionAlert: Do not take רב ששת's words to the רבנן as a real ruling. The גמרא is telling us they were an excuse, so the rule from step 7 is not changed.

phrases.english: There, he was just putting them off,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the story where רב ששת told the רבנן that his daughter's children count as his own.

phrases.english: because Rav Sheshet had become impotent
from Rav Huna's lecture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the source: the story is not a real ruling but an excuse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's words show that grandchildren from one child are enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: His words were only an excuse. His real reason was that he could not have children, so the story proves nothing.

steps.title: רבה asks for the source that grandchildren are like children
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks רבא בר מארי where the rule comes from that grandchildren count like children.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to רבא בר מארי: Where does this idea come from, that the רבנן said grandchildren are like children?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבה wants the פסוק source for the rule that בני בנים הרי הן כבנים, which the whole discussion has been using.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 through 7 all assumed that grandchildren can count in place of children. Now the גמרא goes back and asks for the basis of that idea in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: from where is this matter (what is the source)?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה לְרָבָא בַּר מָארִי:
phrases.english: Rabba said to Rava bar Mari:
From where is this matter
that the Rabbis said
that grandchildren are like children?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new line asking for the source of the idea assumed earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source for the rule that grandchildren count as children.

steps.title: First suggestion: לבן's words to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the source is לבן's statement that יעקב's children are his own children.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it comes from the פסוק 'The daughters are my daughters and the children are my children'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible source. It uses the word 'אילימא' (if you say), which signals that this answer is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לבן calls יעקב's children 'my children,' even though they are really his grandchildren. This seems to show that grandchildren are called children.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a suggestion that will usually be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it is from what is written:
"The daughters are my daughters and the children are my children"
phrases.notes: בראשית 31:43. לבן is speaking to יעקב about יעקב's wives and children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to רבה's question.

steps.title: Rejecting the proof from לבן
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: לבן also said 'the flocks are my flocks,' and they were not really his. He only meant that יעקב got them through him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, when he says 'and the flocks are my flocks,' is that also true?! Rather, he meant 'you got them from me.' Here too, he meant 'you got them from me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from לבן. The same פסוק also calls the sheep 'mine,' and the sheep clearly belonged to יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'my children' meant they are truly his children, then 'my flocks' would have to mean the sheep are truly his, which is false. So לבן just meant 'you have all this because of me.' That gives no proof about grandchildren.

keyTerms.meaning: but if so (introducing a problem with the suggestion)
that you acquired them from me

phrases.english: But if so,
"and the flocks are my flocks" — is that also true?!
phrases.notes: This is the next part of the same פסוק. The sheep were really יעקב's, which he earned by working.

phrases.english: Rather, it means: you acquired them from me;
here too, it means: you acquired them from me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה וְהַצֹּאן צֹאנִי הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from לבן's words is fully rejected.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The same פסוק calls the flocks 'mine,' so the word 'mine' means 'you got it through me,' not real ownership or real parenthood.

steps.title: The real source: מכיר's lawgivers from יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The proof comes from מכיר: his daughter married חצרון from יהודה. The lawgivers of יהודה are called 'from מכיר,' which shows that a daughter's children count as one's own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the source is from here: 'And afterward חצרון came to the daughter of מכיר, the father of גלעד, and she bore him שגוב.' And it says: 'From מכיר came down lawgivers.' And it says: 'יהודה is my lawgiver.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a better proof by joining three פסוקים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מכיר was from שבט מנשה, and the lawgivers were from שבט יהודה. They are called 'from מכיר' only because they came from his daughter, who married חצרון of יהודה. So grandchildren, even through a daughter, are called a person's children.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, it is from here (introducing a better source)
the son of מנשה and father of גלעד

steps.whatToRemember: The source for בני בנים הרי הן כבנים is the lawgivers of יהודה, who are called 'from מכיר' because they descend from his daughter.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from here:
"And afterward Chetzron came
to the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilad
and she bore him Seguv"
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א 2:21. חצרון was from שבט יהודה.

phrases.english: and it is written: "From Machir came down lawgivers"
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:14

phrases.english: and it is written: "Yehuda is my lawgiver."
phrases.notes: תהלים 60:9. So the lawgivers came from יהודה, yet they are still called 'from מכיר.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof with a successful one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leaders from יהודה are called 'from מכיר' because they descend from his daughter. This shows that grandchildren count as children.

steps.title: Our משנה is not like רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה does not follow רבי יהושע. He holds that a man who married and had children when young should marry and have children again when old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not like רבי יהושע. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע says, if a man married a woman in his youth, he should marry a woman in his old age. If he had children in his youth, he should have children in his old age. As it says: 'In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening do not rest your hand, for you do not know which will succeed, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It points out that a different תנא, רבי יהושע, disagrees with the approach of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a man is done once he has the required children. רבי יהושע says he should keep marrying and having children even in old age. He learns this from the פסוק in קהלת: you never know which children will turn out well, so keep 'sowing.'

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that besides the basic מצוה with a set number of children, there is a view that one should keep having children for his whole life.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not like Rabbi Yehoshua,
as it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
If a man married a woman in his youth,
he should marry a woman in his old age.
If he had children in his youth,
he should have children in his old age,
as it is said:
"In the morning sow your seed
phrases.notes: קהלת 11:6. 'Morning' is read as youth and 'evening' as old age.

phrases.english: and in the evening do not rest your hand,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֵינְךָ יוֹדֵעַ אֵי זֶה יִכְשָׁר
phrases.english: for you do not know which will succeed,
this one or that one,
or whether both alike will be good."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, comparing our משנה with the opinion of רבי יהושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, a man should marry and have children even in old age, even if he already had children in his youth.

steps.title: Keep learning and teaching in old age
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that someone who learned Torah and had students when young should keep learning and keep having students when old. He bases this on the פסוק 'In the morning sow your seed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: If a person learned Torah when he was young, he should learn Torah when he is old. If he had students when he was young, he should have students when he is old, as the פסוק says: 'In the morning sow your seed, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. רבי עקיבא takes רבי יהושע's idea about having children again in old age and applies it to Torah learning and teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע read the פסוק 'In the morning sow your seed' as being about children. רבי עקיבא uses the same פסוק for learning and for having students. 'Morning' means youth and 'evening' means old age, so you should not stop just because you already did it once.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
If he learned Torah in his youth,
he should learn Torah in his old age.
If he had students in his youth,
he should have students in his old age,
as it says: "In the morning sow your seed, etc."
phrases.notes: קהלת 11:6. The פסוק goes on: "and in the evening do not hold back your hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לָמַד תּוֹרָה בְּיַלְדוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא that brought רבי יהושע's opinion and applies the same פסוק to Torah and students.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should keep learning Torah and keep having students in old age, even if he already did so in his youth.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's 24,000 students died
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells that רבי עקיבא had 12,000 pairs of students across a large area, and all of them died in one period because they did not treat each other with respect.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: רבי עקיבא had twelve thousand pairs of students, from גבת to אנטיפרס, and all of them died in one period of time, because they did not treat each other with respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a story to show why רבי עקיבא's teaching matters. He had a huge number of students when he was younger, and they all died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the background to the next step. Because his first students died, רבי עקיבא had to find new students later in life, which is exactly what he taught. The reason given for their death is that they did not show each other respect.

phrases.english: They said:
twelve thousand pairs of students
Rabbi Akiva had
from Gevat to Antipatris,
phrases.notes: These are two places in ארץ ישראל. His students filled the whole area between them.

phrases.english: and all of them died in one period,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא נָהֲגוּ כָּבוֹד זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: because they did not treat each other with respect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר אָלֶף זוּגִים תַּלְמִידִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story that shows the background of רבי עקיבא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's 24,000 early students all died in one period because they did not respect one another.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא teaches five new students
steps.stepSummary: After the students died, the world was empty of Torah until רבי עקיבא taught five new students in the South. These five kept Torah alive.
steps.simpleTranslation: The world was empty of Torah until רבי עקיבא came to our Rabbis in the South and taught them his Torah: רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי שמעון, and רבי אלעזר בן שמוע. They are the ones who kept Torah standing at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. In his later years רבי עקיבא found new students, and they saved the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is רבי עקיבא living out his own teaching: he had students when young and new students when old. The second group, though small, carried the Torah to the next generations.

keyTerms.meaning: kept Torah standing, kept it alive

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא practiced what he taught. After losing 24,000 students, he taught five new ones in his old age, and they kept the Torah going.
steps.whyThisMatters: These five students are the main תנאים whose names fill the משנה, so all later Torah learning passes through them.

phrases.english: And the world was desolate,
phrases.notes: He means empty of Torah, since all the students were gone.

phrases.english: until Rabbi Akiva came
to our Rabbis in the South
and taught it to them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן שַׁמּוּעַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, and Rabbi Elazar ben Shamua,

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵם הֵם הֶעֱמִידוּ תּוֹרָה אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה.
phrases.english: and they are the ones who kept Torah standing at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after the first students died, רבי עקיבא raised new ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's five later students (רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, רבי יוסי, רבי שמעון, רבי אלעזר בן שמוע) kept Torah alive.

steps.title: The students died between פסח and שבועות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds that all of רבי עקיבא's students died in the period from פסח until עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: all of them died from פסח until עצרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that tells us exactly when the 'one period' was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said they died 'in one period.' This ברייתא makes it specific: the days between פסח and שבועות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the mourning customs kept during ספירת העומר.

phrases.english: It was taught:
all of them died from Pesach until Atzeres.
phrases.notes: עצרת here means שבועות.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא, כּוּלָּם מֵתוּ מִפֶּסַח וְעַד עֲצֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains which 'one period' the earlier story meant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students died between פסח and שבועות.

steps.title: They died a bad death
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר אבא, or some say רבי חייא בר אבין, says all the students died a bad death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר אבא said, and some say it was רבי חייא בר אבין: All of them died a bad death.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a detail about how the students died. It was a terrible kind of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know when they died. This line adds that the way they died was especially painful. It sets up the next question: what kind of death is meant?

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (it was someone else who said it)

phrases.english: Rav Chama bar Abba said,
and some say Rabbi Chiya bar Avin:
all of them died a bad death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר אַבָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how they died, after the previous step said when.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The students died a bad death.

steps.title: What is a bad death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly 'a bad death' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to explain the term 'bad death.' This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Bad death' is unclear, so the גמרא wants to know which specific death or illness is meant.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the term used in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of death is called a 'bad death'?

steps.title: The bad death was אסכרה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the bad death was אסכרה, a choking disease of the throat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: אסכרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question: the students died of אסכרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אסכרה is a disease that closes the throat and chokes a person, which is known as one of the hardest deaths. This explains the term 'bad death.'

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Askara.
phrases.notes: A disease that swells the throat until a person chokes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע: even after having children, a man should keep marrying and having more children in old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: After the story, the גמרא goes back to the main topic and gives the final ruling. The הלכה follows רבי יהושע from step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said a man is done once he has a son and a daughter. רבי יהושע said he should keep having children even in old age. רב מתנא rules like רבי יהושע, so the obligation to keep having children continues.
steps.whatToRemember: Even after fulfilling פרו ורבו with a son and a daughter, the הלכה like רבי יהושע is that one should keep trying to have more children.
steps.confusionAlert: This ruling goes back to רבי יהושע in step 14 about having children. It is not about the story of רבי עקיבא's students right before it.

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the הלכה question from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע: one should keep having children even after fulfilling the basic מצוה.

steps.title: A man without a wife lacks joy, blessing, and goodness
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחום, quoting רבי חנילאי, teaches that a man with no wife lives without שמחה, ברכה, and טובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחום said in the name of רבי חנילאי: Any man who has no wife lives without joy, without blessing, and without goodness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the topic of having children to sayings about marriage itself. רבי חנילאי lists three good things a man without a wife is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new statement, not an answer to a question. It lists three losses, and the next step will bring a separate פסוק to prove each one.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִילַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Tanchum said that Rabbi Chanilai said:
Any man who does not have a wife
lives without joy,
without blessing, without goodness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי תַּנְחוּם אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִילַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the הלכה about continuing to have children, the גמרא opens a new set of sayings praising marriage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man without a wife lives without joy, blessing, and goodness.

steps.title: Verses that prove each of the three losses
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנילאי brings a פסוק for each of the three: joy, blessing, and goodness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Without joy, as it says: 'You shall rejoice, you and your household.' Without blessing, as it says: 'To bring a blessing to rest on your house.' Without goodness, as it says: 'It is not good for the man to be alone.'
steps.whatsHappening: Each of the three losses from the last step is now backed up by a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first two פסוקים, 'your house' is understood to mean your wife, so joy and blessing come through her. The third פסוק says straight out that being alone is 'not good'.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
Your house; here understood as your wife

phrases.english: Without joy, as it is written:
"And you shall rejoice, you and your household."
phrases.notes: דברים 14:26. Your 'household' here means your wife.

phrases.english: Without blessing, as it is written:
"To cause a blessing to rest on your house."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:30

phrases.english: Without goodness, as it is written:
"It is not good for the man to be alone."
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for each part of the statement in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: The three losses: joy, blessing, goodness.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל they add: without Torah and without a protective wall
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of the West (ארץ ישראל) add two more losses, Torah and a protective wall, each with a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West they say: he is without Torah and without a wall. Without Torah, as it says: 'Is my help not in me, and has wisdom been pushed away from me?' Without a wall, as it says: 'A woman shall surround a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different group of scholars adds two more things a man without a wife lacks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק from איוב, 'help' is read as a wife, and 'wisdom' as Torah. Without the help, the wisdom is lost. A wife who 'surrounds' a man is pictured as a wall that protects him.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
Sound wisdom; here understood as Torah

phrases.english: In the West they say:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is the בבלי's way of saying ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Without Torah, without a wall.
Without Torah, as it is written:
"Is it that I have no help in me,
phrases.notes: איוב 6:13. The 'help' is the wife, like the עזר כנגדו in בראשית.

phrases.english: and that sound wisdom is driven from me?"
Without a wall, as it is written:
"A woman shall go around a man."
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 31:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to רבי חנילאי's list with two more losses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man without a wife is also without Torah and without protection.

steps.title: רבא בר עולא adds: without peace
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר עולא adds that a man without a wife is without שלום, based on a פסוק in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר עולא said: he is without peace, as it says: 'You will know that your tent is at peace, and you will visit your home and not sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: One more אמורא adds one more loss to the list: peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'tent' in the פסוק is read as a man's wife. Peace is connected to the tent, so a man without a wife lacks peace. This same פסוק becomes the base for רבי יהושע בן לוי's next two teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: Your tent; here understood as your wife

steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'visit your home and do not sin' in this פסוק are used in the next two steps to teach practical duties of a husband.

phrases.english: Rava bar Ulla said:
Without peace, as it is written:
"And you shall know that your tent is at peace,
phrases.notes: איוב 5:24. The 'tent' stands for a man's wife.

phrases.english: and you shall visit your home and not sin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final item, peace, to the list of losses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man without a wife is without peace.

steps.title: Neglecting a God-fearing wife makes a man a sinner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that a man who knows his wife is a ירא שמים and does not visit her (is not intimate with her) is called a חוטא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who knows that his wife fears Heaven and does not visit her is called a sinner, as it says: 'You will know that your tent is at peace, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי takes the same פסוק from איוב and draws a practical lesson from it about a husband's duty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'you will visit your home and you will not sin.' He reads it the other way too: if you do not visit, you sin. 'Visit' here is a polite way of saying being intimate with your wife.

keyTerms.meaning: Visits her; a polite term for marital closeness
Etc., the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Anyone who knows about his wife
that she fears Heaven
and he does not visit her
phrases.notes: 'Visit' is a polite way of saying he is not intimate with her.

phrases.english: is called a sinner, as it is said:
"And you shall know that your tent is at peace, etc."
phrases.notes: The key part is the end: 'visit your home and you will not sin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק quoted by רבא בר עולא to teach a husband's obligation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who neglects being close with his God-fearing wife is called a sinner.

steps.title: A husband must be close with his wife before a trip
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds that a man must visit his wife when he is leaving on a journey, from the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: A man must visit his wife when he is about to leave on a journey, as it says: 'You will know that your tent is at peace, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives a second rule from the same פסוק: a husband should be close with his wife before going away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before taught a general duty. This step names a specific time when the duty applies: right before he travels. The next step asks why this needs the פסוק from איוב at all.

keyTerms.meaning: To visit; here, to be close with his wife

steps.whatToRemember: All these sayings show how highly the גמרא values marriage: a wife brings joy, blessing, goodness, Torah, protection, and peace, and a husband has real duties toward her, including closeness before he travels.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
A man is obligated to visit his wife
at the time that he goes out on a journey,
as it is said: "And you shall know that your tent is at peace, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same אמורא on the same פסוק, naming a specific time for the duty.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man must be close with his wife before leaving on a journey.

steps.title: Why bring a new source when one already exists?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי: the rule about visiting one's wife before a journey is already learned from a פסוק in בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we really learn this from here? We already learn it from there: 'And your desire shall be to your husband.' That teaches that a wife longs for her husband when he is leaving on a journey!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יהושע בן לוי needed his פסוק from איוב. A different פסוק already teaches the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 28 says a husband must be with his wife before he travels. The פסוק 'ואל אישך תשוקתך' already shows that a wife longs for her husband at that time. So the second source seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is learned from there (a different source)

phrases.english: Is this derived from here?
It is derived from there:
"And your desire shall be to your husband"
phrases.notes: בראשית 3:16

phrases.english: which teaches that a wife longs for her husband
at the time that he is leaving on a journey!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's source from איוב for visiting one's wife before a journey
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already known from the פסוק in בראשית, so the second source looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The second source is for the time near her period
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the second source teaches the rule even close to the wife's expected period.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is needed only for when it is close to her expected period.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains what the second source adds. It teaches that a husband should be with his wife before a trip even close to her expected period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a couple keeps apart close to the time she expects her period, in case bleeding starts. The פסוק from בראשית alone would not override that. רבי יהושע בן לוי's source teaches that before a journey he should be with her even then.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman's set pattern; the time she expects her period

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the rule about a journey is strong enough to apply even at a time when the couple normally keeps apart.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is needed only for close to her set time.
phrases.notes: Her set time is when she expects her period. Normally a couple keeps apart then.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 29
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the second source to a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second source seemed to repeat what the פסוק in בראשית already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second source teaches that the rule applies even close to her expected period.

steps.title: How close to her period?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much time before her expected period counts as 'close'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much time is 'close'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how much time counts as 'close to her period'. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer uses the word 'close' without giving a measure. The גמרא wants to know the exact amount of time.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the measure of 'close' used in step 30
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long before her expected period counts as 'close'

steps.title: Close means one עונה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that 'close' means one עונה, meaning a day or a night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: One עונה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the measure: one עונה before her expected period counts as 'close'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is half of a full day, so either the daytime or the nighttime. That is the window when a couple normally keeps apart.

keyTerms.meaning: A time period of half a day: either a day or a night

phrases.english: Rava said: An onah.
phrases.notes: An עונה is half a day: either the daytime or the nighttime.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Close' means one עונה, a day or a night.

steps.title: Only for an optional trip, not a trip for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits the rule: it applies to an optional trip, but not to a trip for a מצוה, because he would be distracted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a trip for an optional matter. But for a trip for a מצוה, they would be distracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a limit on the rule of visiting one's wife before a trip. It applies only when the trip is optional, not when it is for a מצוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is traveling for a מצוה, being with his wife right before leaving could leave his mind busy with her. Then he might not focus on the מצוה. So for that kind of trip he does not have to do this.
steps.whatToRemember: Before an optional trip, a husband should be with his wife, even close to her expected period (within one עונה). Before a trip for a מצוה he does not have to, so he will not be distracted.

phrases.english: And this applies only to a trip for an optional matter,
but for a matter of a מצוה, they become preoccupied.
phrases.notes: He means his mind would be busy with his wife, and he might not focus on the מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי לִדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת, אֲבָל לִדְבַר מִצְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule from steps 28 and 30
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of visiting one's wife before a journey applies to an optional trip, not to a trip for a מצוה.

steps.title: Loving and honoring one's family brings a peaceful home
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who loves and honors his wife, guides his children well, and marries them off at the right time will have a peaceful home.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who loves his wife as himself, honors her more than himself, guides his sons and daughters on a straight path, and marries them off close to when they come of age, about him the פסוק says: 'And you shall know that your tent is in peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It lists good ways a man treats his wife and children and promises him a peaceful home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are four behaviors: loving his wife, honoring her even more than himself, raising his children well, and marrying them off at the right age. The reward is the פסוק from איוב about a peaceful tent, meaning a peaceful home. This fits the earlier theme that a man without a wife lacks שלום.

keyTerms.meaning: Like his own body, meaning like himself
Close to their time of maturity

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who loves his wife as himself,
and who honors her more than himself,
and who guides his sons and daughters on an upright path,
and who marries them off close to when they come of age —
about him the verse says:
"And you shall know that your tent is in peace."
phrases.notes: איוב 5:24

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוֹהֵב אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ כְּגוּפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about good family behavior, connected to the earlier theme of a wife bringing שלום
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who loves and honors his wife and raises and marries off his children properly will have a peaceful home.

steps.title: A second list: loving neighbors and relatives
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins a second list: one who loves his neighbors, draws his relatives close, and marries his sister's daughter. The reward comes in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who loves his neighbors, and who draws his relatives close, and who marries his sister's daughter...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts a new list of good behaviors toward the wider family and neighbors. The sentence is not finished here; its פסוק and reward come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first list was about a man's own wife and children. This list widens to neighbors and relatives. Marrying his sister's daughter means marrying someone he already knows and cares for as family.
steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished yet. Do not look for the reward here; the ברייתא gives its פסוק right after this.

phrases.english: One who loves his neighbors,
and who draws his relatives close,
and who marries the daughter of his sister,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second list of behaviors
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loving neighbors, bringing relatives close, and marrying one's sister's daughter are praised. The reward follows in the next part of the text.
